title: runtime /keys: POST /keys ignores unknown body keys (a userId for another user answers 201 and mints a key for the caller); refuse them as the data door does
body:
domain:server#2 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufziCTpjnYbdh76SAWwb

Filing gate: ④ per-layer child of #32169 (p2, filed on the maintainer's 「立卡处理」 after the 2026-11-10 platform test run #32135). Split by the seat on the card thread's phase-1 report, measured on a live showcase at `origin/main` `bb472154` (report: `/mnt/project-files/server-orders/seat2/32169-phase1-report.md`, project files).
Reader: the next `domain:server` seat that claims it.

## What happens

`POST /keys {name, userId: <another user>}` answers **201** and mints the key for the caller; `user_id`, `scopes`, any unknown key are dropped silently. No access widens, but the caller is told nothing. The door is `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts` (~L169, "Whitelist the body"; its header documents the ignore as deliberate). Contrast: the data door refuses an unknown field with `400 INVALID_FIELD` naming it.

## Expected

Refuse any body key outside the accepted set (`name`, `expires_at`, as measured on the door) with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` and `fields[]` naming each key, before any read or write. Update the header comment.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing): a request that answered 201 now answers 400. BREAKING obligations apply. Metadata-protocol: none. Check first-party callers (console, CLI, SDK `keys.create`) send only accepted keys.
Business reason: a client that believes it minted a key for another user (or with scopes) is told it did not.
